2610.08215.title: Learn2Play Bench: How Well Do LLM Agents Learn from Experience in Unfamiliar Environments?
2610.08215.paper_summary: Learning from experience is essential for LLM agents to adapt to unfamiliar and dynmaic environments. Evaluating this ability is therefore important for understanding how effectively agents acquire and use new knowledge. Existing benchmarks have sought to evaluate this ability, but they primarily evaluate tasks whose rules are provided in the instructions or already familiar to pretrained models, making it difficult to distinguish learning from interactions from reasoning with existing knowledge. To address this, we introduce Learn2Play Bench, a benchmark of newly designed text-based games, whose rules are novel or counterintuitive, requiring agents to acquire knowledge through interaction rather than rely solely on pretrained knowledge. These games provide reproducible feedback and automatic scoring, enabling controlled evaluation of learning across repeated attempts. We also vary game instances to test whether agents can apply what they have learned to new situations. Therefore, we evaluate how backbone models, self-evolving methods, and agent harnesses affect agents' learning ability, revealing three findings: (1) Experience retention: Retaining complete records of actions and feedback can support more effective learning than summarizing these experiences into rules or strategies. (2) Human agent gap: Top-performing human players achieve higher peak scores than the evaluated agents. Human explore more varied strategies, and repeat actions less. (3) Harness matters: With the backbone fixed, changing the harness can improve performance while reducing estimated inference cost. Together, these findings provide insights into how LLM agents learn from experience and suggest directions for future work to improve their learning ability. Project website: https://liushiliushi.github.io/learn2play-bench-website/
2610.08215.paper_summary_zh: 學習經驗對於大型語言模型（LLM）代理適應不熟悉和動態環境至關重要。評估這種能力因此對於理解代理如何有效地獲取和使用新知識非常重要。現有的基準測試試圖評估這種能力，但它們主要評估那些在指示中提供規則或對於預訓練模型已經熟悉的任務，這使得從互動中學習與利用現有知識進行推理之間的區分變得困難。為了解決這個問題，我們引入了 Learn2Play Bench，一個新設計的基於文本的遊戲基準，其規則是新穎或反直覺的，要求代理通過互動獲取知識，而不是僅僅依賴預訓練知識。這些遊戲提供可重複的反饋和自動評分，使得在重複嘗試中能夠進行受控的學習評估。我們還變化遊戲實例，以測試代理是否能將所學應用於新情境。因此，我們評估了骨幹模型、自我演化方法和代理工具對代理學習能力的影響，揭示了三個發現：（1）經驗保留：保留完整的行動和反饋記錄可以支持比將這些經驗總結為規則或策略更有效的學習。（2）人類代理差距：表現最佳的人類玩家達到的最高分數高於被評估的代理。人類探索更多樣化的策略，並且重複行動較少。（3）工具重要：在固定骨幹的情況下，改變工具可以提高性能，同時降低預估的推理成本。總體而言，這些發現提供了有關 LLM 代理如何從經驗中學習的見解，並為未來改善其學習能力的工作指明了方向。項目網站：https://liushiliushi.github.io/learn2play-bench-website/
